calls.reason: No deadline and no trustworthy general AI exists to test necessity; ARC Prize's Astra world-model behavior and Google's Genie prototype are adjacent and do not settle whether new architectures are required.
The forecast runs to 2035; Google's agent-systems post and a pre-claim neuro-symbolic review show integration work but do not measure a field-wide shift in main emphasis.
OpenAI's 97% tau2-bench claim is self-reported, while METR's product-task weaknesses and the CLARITY SQL ambiguity study don't isolate intent mapping or set a practical threshold.

Evidence is mixed: METR found reward hacks in about 2% of runs and the system card shows gpt-5-main instruction-hierarchy regressions, but safeguards held in SecureBio tests; no broad measure of recklessness.
GPT-5 was released, and Epoch AI's independent analysis finds large benchmark gains over GPT-4 comparable to the GPT-3 to GPT-4 leap, despite a mixed reception.
Butter-Bench shows GPT-5 well below humans on simple robot delivery tasks, but no evidence addresses the Cicero or driving components of the three-part claim.
